cards.title: Western Europe (500-1500 C.E.)
body: Middle Age (Medieval)- is the period extending from 500-1500 C.E in European history and is marked by the migration of Germanic tribes into Europe to fill the power vacuum created by the fall of the Western Roman Empire. The middle ages is characterized by;
1. A new socio-economic and political system known as Feudalism
2. Retarded economic, cultural and intellectual development
3. Emergence of strong states led by Monarchs
The middle ages is subdivided into 3 periods; Early middle ages, High middle ages and Late middle ages.

cards.title: 1) Early Middle Ages (476-1000)
body: 5th-8th C, various Germanic tribes invaded Europe and created new governments in France, Spain, Italy, England, North Africa and Western Mediterranean.

But by the 6th C, most of their kingdoms were destroyed; the Byzantine Empire destroyed the kingdoms in Italy and North Africa, while the Arabs destroyed the one in Spain. Only the Frankish Kingdom remained.

cards.title: The Frankish Kingdom
body: Was established under the Clovis dynasty and they adopted Roman culture. Their kings and queens had close ties with the Catholic Church. They provided land and received the church’s support in return.
Monasteries were established in the kingdom and were run by monks and nuns. A monk is an individual who leads a life secluded from the world in total devotion to God.

8th C, the Franks were able to defeat the moors (North African Muslims) under the leadership of Charles the Great (Charlemagne) who revived learning and arts. He was crowned ‘Emperor’ in 800 C.E by the Pope. After his death, the kingdom was divided into; A) Western Frankish Kingdom (France)
B) Eastern Frankish Kingdom (Germany)
C) Middle Frankish Kingdom (Italy and Netherlands)
Decline-1) Internal crisis
2) Moor invasion
3) Magyar (people from western Asia) invasion
4) Viking (Germanic tribes of Scandinavia) invasion

cards.title: Feudalism
body: After the decline of Charlemagne’s Empire, people began to seek protection from local landowner aristocrats (nobles and lords), thus an unwritten feudal contract was agreed on between the people and the lords.

Vassalage was the central idea of feudalism where the Vassals served the lords in a military capacity and were in return granted a piece of land that supported their families. This land is known as Fief.

Peasants worked in manors owned by the lords or the fiefs given to the vassals. Manors were agricultural Estates run by lords and worked by peasants known as Serfs. The once free peasants gave up their freedom in return of the protection provided by the lords.

The Serfs were obliged to pay rent to the lords by sharing everything they produced to the lord and pay tithe (a tenth of their products) to the church. Feudalism spread from the Frankish kingdom to England, Germany, Central Europe and Italy by the 11th C.

cards.title: Economy during the Early Middle Ages
body: Their economy was mostly based on agriculture and small local trade which was insufficient because their tools were too primitive. European infrastructure and economy collapsed along with learning and arts.
Europe began to recover after the 10th C as the fall of Charlemagne’s Empire gave rise to new powerful feudal lords in France and Germany, while England was unified under one king.

cards.title: 2) High Middle Ages (1000-1300 C.E)
body: Western Europe emerged from its backwardness as urbanization, military expansion and intellectualism were revived. The progress in the era was caused by;
1. The end of the Moor, Magyar and Viking invasions enabled revival of economy
2. Agricultural Revolution introduced new advances in agricultural technology securing food abundance and the growth of population in the cities.

cards.title: Towns and Cities
body: New cities and towns grew in the Netherlands, Germany, France and Italy, while cities like Rome, Marseille, Paris and Trier grew around the old cities. Most of the Medieval cities had 3 centers; a marketplace, a church or cathedral and a castle.
The manufacture of cloth, metal, shoes and leather products grew in the towns and cities. During the 12th C, artisans organized themselves into business associations known as Guilds.
The Guilds set standards quality for the products produced, specified the methods of production and fixed the prices for the finished goods.

cards.title: Schools and Universities
body: Before the 12th C, Education was only provided by churches and monasteries to young boys until the development city schools which later developed into Universities in the cities of France and Italy. The first European university was in Bologna, while the University of Paris was the first one in Western Europe.

cards.title: Vernacular Literature and Architecture
body: Latin was the most widespread language in Europe during the medieval period; it was used in schools and churches. But in the 12th C, new literature was written in the vernacular languages like Spanish, French, Italian, English and German.
Architecture also grew in the 12th C as many cathedrals in Gothic style were built,
Growth of European Kingdoms- The revival of commerce, growth of cities and economy increased the power of the lords and kings in Europe and gave rise to new monarchies in Europe.

cards.title: England
body: England was invaded by the Germanic tribes of Angles and Saxons and fell under Anglo-Saxon kings after it was united by King Alfred the Great in the 9th C.

13th C, nobles rebelled against King John because they hated the increasing power of the kings and John was forced to sign the document of rights known as the Magna Carta (the Great Charter) in 1215. This limited the power of the kings and gave rise to the Parliament in the 13th C. The Parliament had the right to levy taxes and pass laws; it was composed of two houses; the House of the Lords and the House of Commons.

cards.title: The French Kingdom
body: Emerged from the Western Frankish Kingdom under the Capetian dynasty of Hugh Capet in 987 C.E.
During the reign of King Philip II (1180-1223), the French monarchy grew and French lands under the English rule were recovered. France became the largest monarchial state in Europe in 1300.

In 1302, King Philip IV set up a Parliament known as Estates General consisting 3 Estates; the first Estate was composed of the clergy, the second was of the nobles and the third of townspeople and peasants.

cards.title: The Catholic Church
body: Since the 5th C, the popes have had both spiritual and political powers and controlled all the affairs of the church and set up territories in central Italy known as the Papal States. Bishops were appointed by the kings of the Eastern Frankish (Holy Roman Empire) and were obliged to carry out feudal and military services.

Conflict arose when the Church wanted to appoint its own officials; it was solved by the Concordat of Worms (1122). The agreement stated that the church officials were to be appointed by both the church and the kings.

cards.title: 3) Late Middle Ages (1300-1450 C.E )
body: The period is characterized by;
A) Plague- the Black Death
B) Economic decline
C) Decline of the Catholic Church
D) Political instability

cards.title: A) The Black Death
body: The Black Death (Bubonic plague) was the worst natural disaster in European history spread by infested black rats brought into Sicily from the Black Sea by Italian merchants in the 1347. It quickly spread into Italy, France (1348), Germany, the Low countries (modern Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands), England (1349), Scandinavia, Russia and Eastern Europe (1351).

Out of the total European population of 70 million, 38 million died in 1347-1351. In England, Germany and Italy, entire villages disappeared. The plague brought the outbreak of anti-Semitism as people accused the Jews of poisoning the wells.

cards.title: B) The Hundred Years War (1337-1453)
body: A series of wars between France and England caused by territorial dispute. The war affected both their economies and societies. England faced human and economic losses; it also faced the War of Roses, a civil war caused as the nobles fought to control the monarchy until the coming of the Tudor dynasty in 1485.
In the 15th C, new European monarchies were established in France, England and Spain after recovering from the 14th C economic decline and civil wars.

cards.title: Model answer: characteristics of the Middle Ages
cards.problem: (Exam question) What were the main characteristics of the Middle Ages in Western Europe (500–1500 C.E.)?

steps.text: Define the period: 500–1500 C.E., starting when Germanic tribes moved in to fill the power vacuum left by the fall of the Western Roman Empire.
Characteristic 1: a new socio-economic and political system – feudalism, built on vassals serving lords in return for land.
Characteristic 2: slow (retarded) economic, cultural and intellectual development.
Characteristic 3: the emergence of strong states led by monarchs; the period is divided into Early, High and Late Middle Ages.

cards.answer: Feudalism, slow economic and intellectual development, and the rise of strong monarchies – in a period that followed the fall of Rome and the Germanic migrations.

lessons.title: The Byzantine Empire and the Crusades (500-1500 C.E)

cards.title: The Byzantine Empire and the Crusades (500-1500 C.E)
body: The Eastern Roman Empire with its center at Constantinople (modern Istanbul) existed after the fall of the Roman Empire. King Justinian restored the Roman Empire in the Mediterranean including Italy, parts of Spain, North Africa, Asia Minor, Palestine and Syria in 552.
Architecture grew under Justinian, the most famous structure was Hagia Sophia (the church of Holy Wisdom 532-537). After his death, the Empire was lost to the Lombards of Italy.

cards.title: From Eastern Roman Empire to Byzantine Empire
body: The Eastern Roman Empire was challenged by the Islamic forces who occupied Syria and Palestine in the 7th C and the Bulgarians who had created a strong Empire in 679 limiting the empire into eastern Balkans and Asia Minor, this empire was called the Byzantine Empire.

It was a Greek-Christian state with Greek as their official language and Orthodox Christianity as the official religion. They believed the emperor was chosen by God and had absolute power. The Patriarch (head of the Eastern Orthodox Church) was chosen by the emperor.

Economy- Agriculture was the main source of wealth; they produced grain, olive oil, wine and cheese. Trade was conducted between Asia and Europe, they imported Silk (China), Spices (Southeast Asia and India), ivory (India), wheat and fur (Russia) and Flax and honey (Balkans). They exported cotton, glassware, timber and silk.
Height-The Empire expanded under the Macedonians from 867 to 1081, economy and power was restored.
Decline 1. Weak Rulers
2. Civil war between military rulers and the aristocrats in the 11th C
3. Schism- the split of Christianity into the Catholic and the Orthodox Churches
4. Seljuk (Turkish) invasion Seljuks in 1071. Emperor Alexis I had to ask for European help.

cards.title: The Crusades
body: The Crusades were a series of religious wars fought between Muslims and Christians caused by the Seljuk invasion of the Byzantine Empire and Alexis’s plea for Christian help from Europe. European Knights joined the war because they were motivated by; religious feelings, adventure, to gain wealth and title, and create trade opportunities.

1) The first Crusade (1096-1099)-3 French warrior groups went to Constantinople and set up 4 states in Antioch (1098), Edessa, Tripoli and Jerusalem (1099), this resulted in the growth of the port cities of Geona, Pisa and Venice.
2) The Second Crusade (1147-1149)- the Muslims recaptured Edessa in the 1140s, but the crusade failed.

3) The Third Crusade (1189-1192)- begun after the Muslims controlled Jerusalem led by commander Saladin in 1187. European forces under Emperor Frederick Barbarossa (Germany), Richard I the Lionhearted (England), and Philip II Augustus (France). Frederick’s forces drowned in a river, Philip went back home and Richard reached an agreement with Saladin allowing Christian pilgrimage to Jerusalem.

4) The Fourth Crusade- was initiated by Pope Innocent III and the crusade focused on sacking Constantinople in 1204. The Byzantines recovered the city in 1261 and reestablished the Empire in a reduced size.
The Fifth and Sixth Crusades aimed to control the Holy Lands but they both failed.

cards.title: Positive Effects of the Crusades
body: 1) Italian cities and ports grew from transporting supplies to the Byzantine Empire by replacing Muslim merchants
2) It helped break down Feudalism, serfs were freed as the lords and kings were busy fighting.
3) Nation-States of Portugal, Spain, England and France grew due to the wealth obtained from trade.
4) Learning was revived as the Greco-Roman books of the Muslims were taken to Europe by the Crusaders

cards.title: Negative Effects of the Crusades
body: 1) Human and material losses on both sides
2 Anti-Zionism sentiments grew in Europe

cards.q: The war fought b/n European Christians and Muslims from 11-13^{th} C.AD to liberate Jerusalem known as:
cards.why:
**Step 1:** From the lesson: “The Crusades were a series of religious wars fought between Muslims and Christians caused by the Seljuk invasion of the Byzantine Empire and Alexis’s plea for Christian help from Europe.”

**Step 2:** The **Crusades** were a series of religious wars initiated, supported, and sometimes directed by the Latin Church in the medieval period, with the objective of recovering the Holy Land (Jerusalem) from Islamic rule.

**Step 3:** So the answer is E) Crusade war.

cards.q: One of the effects of the crusades was the ...

options.C: weakening of kings and the growing stronger of nobles.

cards.why:
**Step 1:** The Crusades led to the revival of trade and learning in Europe as contact with the Byzantine and Islamic worlds increased. Politically, they weakened feudalism (nobles died or sold land to join) and strengthened kings, paving the way for centralized nation-states.

**Step 2:** So the answer is E) A and D..

**Step 2:** The Eastern Roman Empire, also known as the Byzantine Empire, had its capital at **Constantinople** (modern-day Istanbul), founded by Emperor Constantine the Great in 330 AD.

**Step 3:** So the answer is B) Constantinople.

questions.q: The High middle age in European history was characterized by:
questions.label: 13. The High middle age in European history was characterized by:
why: Answer B: Urbanization

From the lesson: “Middle Age (Medieval)- is the period extending from 500-1500 C.E in European history and is marked by the migration of Germanic tribes into Europe to fill the power vacuum created by the fall of the Western Roman Empire.”
The High Middle Ages (c. 1000–1300) was a period of growth, including urbanization and the rise of trade. The Black Death and Hundred Years' War occurred in the Late Middle Ages (after 1300).
So the answer is B) Urbanization.

questions.q: The medieval period in western Europe was characterized by:
questions.label: 14. The medieval period in western Europe was characterized by:

options.D: Emergence of strong states led by monarch.

why: Answer E: All except C

From the lesson: “Middle Age (Medieval)- is the period extending from 500-1500 C.E in European history and is marked by the migration of Germanic tribes into Europe to fill the power vacuum created by the fall of the Western Roman Empire.”

The Medieval period (Middle Ages) featured feudalism and a decline in classical learning (often called the Dark Ages). Capitalism, however, emerged later during the Renaissance and the Early Modern period. Strong centralized monarchies also began to form towards the end of the Middle Ages.
So the answer is E) All except C.

The **Bubonic Plague** (Black Death) occurred in the 14th century, which is considered the **Late Middle Ages**, marking the end of the High Middle Ages prosperity.

From the lesson: “Middle Age (Medieval)- is the period extending from 500-1500 C.E in European history and is marked by the migration of Germanic tribes into Europe to fill the power vacuum created by the fall of the Western Roman Empire.”
The Western Roman Empire collapsed in 476 CE after continuous invasions by various Germanic tribes such as the Visigoths, Vandals, and Franks.
So the answer is A) Germanic tribes..

questions.q: Historical period Characterized by **Feudalism** was:
questions.label: 17. Historical period Characterized by **Feudalism** was:
why: Answer C: Middle Ages
From the lesson: “The middle ages is subdivided into 3 periods;”

Feudalism was the dominant social, political, and economic system in medieval Europe (Middle Ages), roughly from the 9th to the 15th centuries. It was based on land ownership and the relationship between lords and vassals.
So the answer is C) Middle Ages.

questions.q: Identify which of the following is not the state that was conquered by first crusaders
questions.label: 18. Identify which of the following is not the state that was conquered by first crusaders
why: Answer E: C and D

The First Crusade resulted in the establishment of the Crusader states of Edessa, Antioch, Tripoli, and Jerusalem. Lahore and Baghdad were not part of these conquests; Lahore is in modern-day Pakistan and Baghdad was the capital of the Abbasid Caliphate.
So the answer is E) C and D.
